assessment: Grande and colleagues provide important new insights into how different regions of the entorhinal cortex functionally interact with specific cortical brain areas and how, in turn, subregions of the entorhinal cortex interact with the hippocampus during 'scene' and 'object' processing. The study is well-motivated, well-designed, and provides convincing evidence using appropriate methodology. This paper is relevant to cognitive neuroscientists with an interest in the entorhinal cortex – hippocampal pathways and 'scene' and 'object' representation in the medial temporal lobe.
